specPoints.text: understand the roles of FSH and LH in the menstrual cycle

primer.text: Oestrogen and progesterone get the headlines, but two brain signals run the cycle's opening act. FSH wakes an egg follicle and switches on oestrogen; once oestrogen peaks, LH fires and ovulation follows, handing the ovary its progesterone job. This note tracks both pituitary hormones and the eight-step relay they drive.

lessons.title: Pituitary Signals and the Ovarian Relay
sourceHeadings: Roles of FSH & LH in the Menstrual Cycle
lessons.opening: FSH and LH leave the pituitary gland in sequence: FSH matures an egg follicle and starts oestrogen release, and once oestrogen peaks, LH triggers ovulation and the follicle's conversion into the progesterone-producing corpus luteum.
keyPoints: FSH and LH are hormones made by the pituitary gland, which sits in the brain.
FSH starts an egg maturing inside the ovary and switches on oestrogen release.
LH is released when oestrogen peaks, causing ovulation to occur.
LH then pushes the ovary into its progesterone-producing phase.
The follicle becomes the corpus luteum, whose progesterone holds the lining until the placenta can take over.

low.restatement: FSH ripens the egg and raises oestrogen; LH then bursts the follicle and starts progesterone.
low.analogy: A two-button launch: button one fuels the rocket (FSH), button two opens the pad gates (LH).
low.examPointer: Anchor each hormone to its two effects — FSH matures plus stimulates oestrogen; LH ovulates plus starts progesterone.

medium.restatement: The relay is feedback-driven: rising oestrogen first suppresses FSH, then at peak levels it triggers the LH surge, so the pituitary and ovary trade control of the cycle in strict order until pregnancy, when the placenta maintains progesterone production itself.
medium.analogy: A thermostat hand-off: one signal heats the room until a threshold flips control to a second system.
medium.examPointer: Link high oestrogen to the LH release — the trigger order is the discriminating fact.

check.stem: Which gland releases FSH and LH?

options.text: The pituitary gland in the brain
options.explanation: Correct — this follows directly from the definition.
The ovary responds to FSH and LH; it does not release them.
The uterus is the implantation site, not a hormone source for these two.
The thyroid manages metabolic rate, not the cycle's pituitary hormones.

check.stem: What does FSH do in the ovary?

options.text: It starts an egg maturing inside the ovary and switches on oestrogen release
options.explanation: Yes — the mechanism works exactly this way.
Ovulation is LH's job.
Progesterone maintains the lining.

options.text: It breaks down the corpus luteum
options.explanation: The corpus luteum breaks down when progesterone falls.

check.stem: Which event follows the oestrogen peak?

options.text: LH release, which causes ovulation to occur
options.explanation: Correct — this matches the account taught above.
FSH comes from the pituitary, and it rises early, not after the peak.
Menstruation follows progesterone's fall much later.
The corpus luteum forms after ovulation first.

check.stem: Besides causing ovulation, what second role does LH play?

options.text: It nudges the ovary into making progesterone
options.explanation: Right — this is the account the lesson teaches.
FSH matures the follicle.

options.text: It releases oestrogen from the pituitary
options.explanation: Oestrogen is ovarian, and the pituitary does not make it.
Lining shedding follows progesterone's fall, not LH directly.

check.stem: A woman becomes pregnant just after ovulation. Who keeps progesterone production running in the first weeks, and who takes over later?

options.text: The corpus luteum first, then the placenta once it develops
options.explanation: Right — the other options each misplace a concept.
Both are pituitary signals, not progesterone sources.
The pituitary signals but does not sustain pregnancy progesterone.
The lining responds to progesterone; it does not produce the pregnancy supply.

check.stem: State the full name of FSH and its gland of origin.
check.modelAnswer: FSH is follicle-stimulating hormone, released from the pituitary gland.

check.stem: State the event that LH causes in the ovary.
check.modelAnswer: LH causes ovulation to occur and triggers progesterone production.

check.stem: Explain why high oestrogen levels lead to a surge of LH.
check.modelAnswer: Once oestrogen has reached its peak, that high level triggers the pituitary to release LH, so ovulation follows the follicle's full maturation.

check.stem: A drug blocks LH receptors in the ovary. Predict two cycle events that would fail.
check.modelAnswer: Ovulation would not occur, and the ovary would not be stimulated to produce progesterone, so the corpus luteum stage would fail.

glossary.definition: Follicle-stimulating hormone from the pituitary gland that starts egg maturing and oestrogen release.
Luteinising hormone from the pituitary gland that triggers ovulation and progesterone production.
The brain gland that releases FSH and LH.
The ovarian structure that holds the maturing egg and produces oestrogen.
